newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS REACHES 5-0 WITH SECOND COMPLETE GAME FOR JAYS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS REACHES 5-0 WITH SECOND COMPLETE GAME FOR JAYS.

text.p: It's beginning to look as if 34-year-old Roger Clemens is worth the huge free agent contract he signed to join the Toronto Blue Jays in the off-season.
Clemens fired his second complete of the young season to lead Toronto to a 3-1 win over the Detroit Tigers and raise his record to 5-0 on Monday.

Clemens, who signed a three-year, $24.75 million contract to leave Boston after 13 years as ace of the Red Sox staff, allowed one run and five hits. He did not issue a walk and struck out 10 to lower his league-leading ERA to 1.58 with his 103rd career complete game.
Carlos Garcia stroked a two-run double in the fifth inning to give Clemens all the support he would need.
"I'm used to (tight games), in Boston I had a ton of nail-biters," Clemens said. "I'm not worrried about my career wins and losses, I'm worried about the playoffs and the World Series."
The Tigers pushed across their only run in the second on Melvin Nieves' RBI triple. The Jays added an insurance run in the eighth when Otis Nixon stole third and scored on Joe Carter's sacrifice fly.
Omar Olivares (1-2) gave up three runs and seven hits over 7 1/3 innings to take the loss. The Tigers have scored a total of just six runs for Olivares in his last four starts.
In Boston, Kevin Appier pitched a five-hitter and Jay Bell homered and drove in two runs as the Kansas Royals blanked the Red Sox 2-0.
Appier (4-1) walked one and struck out seven for his league-leading third complete game of the season and 10th career shutout. He allowed only one runner past first base.
"Appier right now is better than he's ever been," said Kansas City manager Bob Boone.
Chris Hammond (1-1) pitched eight innings, allowing two runs and seven hits with three walks and nine strikeouts.
In Baltimore, Tim Salmon homered and drove in four and Eddie Murray highlighted a four-run first with a two-run single as the Anaheim Angels beat the Orioles 7-2.
Salmon ignited the four-run first against Scott Kamieniecki (2-1) with an RBI single. Murray later singled to centre, scoring Jim Leyritz and Salmon for a 3-0 lead.
Salmon extended the cushion to 7-2 in the eighth with a three-run homer off reliever Terry Mathews.
Jason Dickson (5-1) allowed two runs and six hits over 6-1/3 innings for the win.
In New York, Greg Swindell retired 12 straight batters in relief Pat Meares had three hits and three RBI as the Minnesota Twins edged the Yankees 9-8.
Pat Meares and Chuck Knoblauch hit back-to-back homers in the fifth as the Twins rallied from a 5-1 deficit. Terry Steinbach added a solo shot for Minnesota.
Swindell (2-1) kept the Yanks off the bases from the fifth through eighth innings, allowing one run, two hits and no walks.
Red-hot Tino Martinez, who had two homers Sunday to reach 40 RBI, led off the second with his 13th homer for New York. Derek Jeter added a three-run shot for the Yanks in the ninth.
In Milwaukee, Jose Valentin came off the disabled list and delivered a bases-loaded triple in a six-run fifth inning that sparked the Brewers to an 11-7 win over the Oakland Athletics.
Jeromy Burnitz added three hits, three runs and two RBI for the Brewers.
Oakland rallied within 8-7 in the top of the seventh, but Gerald Williams hit a two-run homer in the bottom half and Burnitz added an RBI single in the eighth for Milwaukee.
Scott Karl (1-5) gave up three runs and five hits in five innings for his first win.
Scott Brosius and Mark McGwire homered for Oakland.
